=== SRIS_voice_ack : REUSABLE PHONE-CALL ESCALATION SUBFLOW ===

READING NOTE
  Variable references below are written WITHOUT their leading dollar
  sign - as exec, verdict.message and so on. Shuffle substitutes
  variables inside every node parameter INCLUDING this text, so writing
  them properly here makes this note emit bogus
  "shuffle_variable_error: Failed finding ..." lines on every run.

WHAT IT DOES
  Calls a human by phone until one of them presses a key, then returns
  proof of who acknowledged. Call it from any workflow that needs an
  out-of-band, acknowledged page.

HOW TO CALL IT
  Add a Subflow node in the calling workflow, point it at this workflow,
  tick "Wait for results", and pass a JSON execution argument:

    {"incident_ref": "SBG-20260803-0412",
     "message": "Impossible travel detected for Super Bock Group",
     "numbers": ["+351911111111", "+351922222222"]}

  Inside this workflow that argument arrives as the exec variable.

WHAT IT RETURNS
  Each Eval emits the verdict directly; the one that ends the
  ladder is the result ->
    {"acknowledged": true/false, "acked_by": "+351...", "digit": "1",
     "attempt": 3, "elapsed_seconds": 214, "attempts": [...],
     "input_source": "exec" | "fallback_oncall_numbers"}

  Callers branch on:  <subflow_node>.message.acknowledged  equals  true

EXPECTED DEBUG MESSAGES - THESE ARE NOT FAULTS
  1. Parse_Input: "Failed finding 'exec'" on a MANUAL run.
     There is no execution argument when you press Run by hand, so the
     node falls back to the oncall_numbers workflow variable and
     reports input_source = fallback_oncall_numbers. The message
     disappears when a real caller invokes this as a subflow. To
     silence it in a manual test, use Run with an execution argument
     and paste the example JSON above.

  2. (Fixed in v3) There is no collector node any more, so the
     old 'Failed finding eval_N.message' emails are gone. Each
     Eval computes the whole verdict from Parse_Input plus its
     own Poll and ends its branch with its own Telegram node.
     Do NOT add a node that reads several Evals at once - that
     reintroduces the errors.

OUTCOME CLASSIFICATION (v4)
  acknowledged=False alone does not say why. outcome tells you:
    acknowledged   someone pressed the key
    no_answer      calls reached the network, nobody picked up
    busy           every call came back busy
    voicemail      answered by a machine, never a human
    not_delivered  no carrier response at all - the PHONE CHANNEL is
                   broken, not the on-call. Seen 2026-08-07 when calls
                   sat at 'Completed' with a null status_code for 30
                   minutes before the carrier drained the queue.
    mixed          some delivered, some not - non-answer is unproven
    no_records     history returned nothing; suspect auth or the query
  This lives in the message, not in branch conditions, on purpose: three
  mutually exclusive edges would mean an unforeseen outcome fires no
  edge and the alert vanishes silently.

THE LADDER (8 stages, ~9 minutes worst case)
  Stages 1-5  -> numbers[0]  (primary)
  Stages 6-8  -> numbers[1]  (secondary)
  70 seconds between calls. Stops the moment anyone presses a key.
  Worst case is 8 calls, about EUR 0.40.

WHY THE POLL LOOKS 'WRONG' - DO NOT OPTIMISE THIS
  Every Poll node queries the WHOLE incident window, not just its own
  call. So an acknowledgment ClickSend was slow to record during stage 2
  is still caught by the stage 3 poll, before stage 4 dials. Late acks
  are absorbed rather than lost, and no measured propagation delay is
  needed. Filtering a Poll by a single message_id breaks this.

WHAT COUNTS AS AN ACK - THE THING MOST LIKELY TO BE BROKEN LATER
  ClickSend returns digits as JSON null when nobody pressed a key -
  NOT the blank string the docs claim. Verified 2026-08-03 against real
  records: a Busy call and an unanswered call both returned null; the
  acknowledged call returned "1".

  A naive `str(digits) != ""` test evaluates str(None) == "None", which
  is non-empty. EVERY FAILED CALL WOULD REGISTER AS ACKNOWLEDGED, the
  ladder would stop at the first busy signal, and nobody would be woken.
  is_ack() in the Eval nodes is the ONLY place an ack is decided.

  Also: status is NOT an ack. The acknowledged test call reported
  status "Sent", not "Delivered". Only `digits` counts.

BRANCH TOPOLOGY WARNING
  Shuffle allows only ONE edge per (source, destination) pair - a second
  one is silently dropped on import. That is why the last Eval node has
  a single UNCONDITIONAL edge to Verdict rather than true/false edges.
  Adding a conditional twin would delete the other and the subflow would
  return nothing when nobody answers.

SETUP REQUIRED
  Workflow variable clicksend_basic_auth = base64 of "username:apikey":
      echo -n 'user@example.com:APIKEY' | base64
  Never paste the raw API key into a node.

KNOWN OPEN ITEM
  ClickSend caller ID is not stable (+12012791392 and +12012665159 both
  observed), so it cannot be whitelisted for Do Not Disturb bypass.
  A dedicated number would improve the wake-up rate more than any
  retry tuning in this workflow.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# PARSE_INPUT - validate the caller's argument and build the ladder.
#
# Fails LOUDLY on bad input. A malformed phone number at 04:00 is a
# silent non-page, which is worse than a crashed workflow: the crash
# gets noticed, the silence does not.
#
# Pre-builds all 8 call payloads here so the Call nodes stay dumb
# one-liners and every payload decision lives in one reviewable place.
#
# EXPECTED: "shuffle_variable_error: Failed finding 'exec'" on a manual
# run. There is no execution argument unless a caller passes one, so
# the reference below stays unsubstituted, json.loads fails, and we
# fall back to the oncall_numbers workflow variable. Harmless in a
# test - but the fallback is recorded as input_source so that a
# REAL page can never quietly ring the default on-call while everyone
# assumes it used the numbers the caller supplied.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
import json, time, re

raw = r"""$exec"""

input_source = "exec"
try:
    args = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip() else {}
except Exception:
    args = {}

if not isinstance(args, dict):
    args = {}
if not args:
    input_source = "fallback_oncall_numbers"

incident_ref = str(args.get("incident_ref") or ("SRIS-%d" % int(time.time())))
# Keep the ref clean: it becomes part of custom_string and is read aloud.
incident_ref = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9\-]", "", incident_ref)[:24]

message = str(args.get("message") or "Critical S R I S alert.")

numbers = args.get("numbers")
if isinstance(numbers, str):
    try:
        numbers = json.loads(numbers)
    except Exception:
        numbers = [numbers]
if not numbers:
    # Fall back to the workflow-level on-call list.
    input_source = "fallback_oncall_numbers"
    try:
        numbers = json.loads(r"""$oncall_numbers""")
    except Exception:
        numbers = []

numbers = [str(n).strip() for n in numbers if str(n).strip()]
bad = [n for n in numbers if not re.match(r"^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$", n)]

if not numbers or bad:
    out = {"fatal": True,
           "error": "No valid E.164 numbers. bad=%s all=%s" % (bad, numbers),
           "incident_ref": incident_ref,
           "input_source": input_source}
    print(json.dumps(out))
else:
    now = int(time.time())
    primary = numbers[0]
    secondary = numbers[1] if len(numbers) > 1 else numbers[0]
    ladder = [primary] * 5 + [secondary] * 3

    def body_for(attempt, to):
        # custom_string is unique PER ATTEMPT but prefixed with the
        # incident ref, so a Poll can match the whole incident with a
        # startswith() while the audit trail stays attempt-accurate.
        cs = "%s:%d:%s" % (incident_ref, attempt, to.lstrip("+"))
        # Digits are spaced with commas so a half-asleep listener can
        # follow them; ClickSend renders a comma as a short pause.
        ref_digits = ", ".join(list(incident_ref[-4:]))
        spoken = ("Alert. %s. Reference, %s. Press 1 to acknowledge. "
                  "Again, press 1 to acknowledge." % (message, ref_digits))
        return {"messages": [{
            "to": to,
            "body": spoken[:290],          # 300 chars = 1 message credit
            "lang": "en-gb",
            "voice": "female",
            "country": "PT",
            "custom_string": cs,
            "require_input": 1,            # capture the keypress
            "machine_detection": 1,        # leave voicemail, never an ack
            "source": "shuffle-sris",
        }]}

    out = {
        "fatal": False,
        "incident_ref": incident_ref,
        "input_source": input_source,
        "started_at": now,
        "date_from": now - 120,
        "date_to": now + 3600,
        "ladder": ladder,
    }
    for i, to in enumerate(ladder, start=1):
        out["call_%d_body" % i] = body_for(i, to)

    print(json.dumps(out))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------
# EVAL_1 - has anyone acknowledged, and if not, WHY not?
#
# SELF-CONTAINED BY DESIGN. References only Parse_Input and its own Poll,
# never another Eval. Shuffle substitutes variables textually before
# execution, so a reference to a node that did not run raises an error
# and emails you. A convergent collector node can never avoid that, so
# there isn't one - each Eval emits the complete verdict and ends its
# own branch.
#
# WHY THE OUTCOME CLASSIFICATION EXISTS
# "Nobody pressed 1" and "no call ever reached a handset" both leave
# acknowledged=False, but they need opposite responses at 04:00. One
# means go find the on-call; the other means the phone channel is broken
# and the on-call may be sitting there unaware. Observed 2026-08-07:
#   status_code 201 / Sent      -> reached the network, real disposition
#   status_code 301 / Failed    -> Busy, reached the carrier
#   status_code null/ Completed -> handed off, NO carrier response at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------
import json, time

STAGE = 1
REF = "$parse_input.message.incident_ref"
ACK_DIGIT = "$ack_digit".strip()


def load(raw):
    try:
        v = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip() else None
        return v if isinstance(v, dict) else None
    except Exception:
        return None


plan = load(r"""$parse_input.message""") or {}

raw = r"""$poll_1"""
try:
    resp = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else raw
except Exception:
    resp = {}

rows = (((resp or {}).get("body") or {}).get("data") or {})
rows = rows.get("data") if isinstance(rows, dict) else rows
if not isinstance(rows, list):
    rows = []


def is_ack(rec):
    """THE ONLY PLACE AN ACK IS DECIDED. See the README node.

    ClickSend sends digits as JSON null when no key was pressed, so the
    None check MUST come before any string coercion. str(None) is "None"
    - truthy and non-empty - which would pass Busy and undelivered calls
    as acknowledgments and stop the ladder with nobody woken up.

    Verified against real records:
        Busy call          -> digits = None   -> NOT an ack
        No carrier reply   -> digits = None   -> NOT an ack
        Key pressed        -> digits = "1"    -> ack
    """
    cs = rec.get("custom_string") or ""
    if not cs.startswith(REF):
        return False                # belongs to another incident
    d = rec.get("digits")
    if d is None:                   # null == nobody pressed anything
        return False
    d = str(d).strip()
    if not d:                       # blank string, if they ever ship one
        return False
    if ACK_DIGIT and d != ACK_DIGIT:
        return False                # pressed a key, but not the ack key
    return True


mine = [r for r in rows if (r.get("custom_string") or "").startswith(REF)]
hits = [r for r in mine if is_ack(r)]


def classify(rec):
    """delivered / busy / no_response - based on what the carrier said."""
    code = rec.get("status_code")
    code = str(code).strip() if code is not None else ""
    status = str(rec.get("status") or "").strip().lower()
    if not code:
        # 'Completed' with a null status_code means ClickSend handed the
        # call to the network and never got a result back.
        return "no_response"
    if code.startswith("2") or status == "sent":
        return "delivered"
    return "busy"


for r in mine:
    r["_class"] = classify(r)

total = len(mine)
delivered = sum(1 for r in mine if r["_class"] == "delivered")
busy = sum(1 for r in mine if r["_class"] == "busy")
noresp = sum(1 for r in mine if r["_class"] == "no_response")
voicemail = sum(1 for r in mine
                if str(r.get("machine_detected") or "0") not in ("0", "None", ""))

attempts = [{"custom_string": r.get("custom_string"),
             "to": r.get("to"),
             "status": r.get("status"),
             "status_code": r.get("status_code"),
             "status_text": r.get("status_text"),
             "digits": r.get("digits"),
             "machine_detected": r.get("machine_detected"),
             "date_added": r.get("date_added"),
             "outcome": r["_class"]} for r in mine]

calls_line = "%d delivered, %d busy, %d no carrier response" % (
    delivered, busy, noresp)
if voicemail:
    calls_line += " (%d hit voicemail)" % voicemail

started = plan.get("started_at") or int(time.time())

out = {
    "incident_ref": plan.get("incident_ref"),
    "input_source": plan.get("input_source"),
    "acknowledged": False,
    "acked_by": None,
    "digit": None,
    "attempt": None,
    "acked_at": None,
    "elapsed_seconds": int(time.time()) - int(started),
    "stages_run": STAGE,
    "calls_placed": total,
    "delivered": delivered,
    "busy": busy,
    "no_response": noresp,
    "voicemail": voicemail,
    "calls_line": calls_line,
    "attempts": attempts,
}

if hits:
    h = hits[0]
    # Which call was answered? Read it off the custom_string
    # (ref:attempt:msisdn) rather than assuming it was this stage - a
    # late-recorded ack from an earlier call is caught by this poll too.
    attempt_no = STAGE
    parts = (h.get("custom_string") or "").split(":")
    if len(parts) >= 2 and parts[-2].isdigit():
        attempt_no = int(parts[-2])
    out.update({
        "acknowledged": True,
        "acked_by": h.get("to"),
        "digit": str(h.get("digits")).strip(),
        "attempt": attempt_no,
        "acked_at": h.get("date_added"),
        "message_id": h.get("message_id"),
        "outcome": "acknowledged",
        "outcome_line": "ACKNOWLEDGED by %s on call %s" % (
            h.get("to"), attempt_no),
    })
elif total == 0:
    # No history rows at all. Not "nobody answered" - we cannot even see
    # the calls. Auth, wrong window, or the API is down.
    out["outcome"] = "no_records"
    out["outcome_line"] = ("NO CALL RECORDS - ClickSend history returned "
                           "nothing for this reference. Check auth and the "
                           "history query, not the on-call.")
elif noresp == total:
    out["outcome"] = "not_delivered"
    out["outcome_line"] = ("NOT DELIVERED - %d of %d calls got no carrier "
                           "response. Telephony problem, NOT the on-call. "
                           "They may never have heard a ring." % (noresp, total))
elif noresp:
    out["outcome"] = "mixed"
    out["outcome_line"] = ("MIXED - %d delivered but %d got no carrier "
                           "response. Partial telephony failure, treat the "
                           "non-answer as unproven." % (delivered, noresp))
elif voicemail and voicemail >= delivered and delivered:
    out["outcome"] = "voicemail"
    out["outcome_line"] = ("VOICEMAIL - calls were answered by a machine, "
                           "never a human. %d of %d." % (voicemail, total))
elif busy == total and total:
    out["outcome"] = "busy"
    out["outcome_line"] = ("ALL BUSY - %d of %d calls returned busy. Line "
                           "engaged or the phone is rejecting." % (busy, total))
else:
    out["outcome"] = "no_answer"
    out["outcome_line"] = ("NO ANSWER - %d of %d calls reached the network, "
                           "none acknowledged. The on-call did not pick up."
                           % (delivered, total))

print(json.dumps(out))

# acknowledged=False, but they need opposite responses at 04:00. One
# means go find the on-call; the other means the phone channel is broken
# and the on-call may be sitting there unaware. Observed 2026-08-07:

#   status_code 301 / Failed    -> Busy, reached the carrier
#   status_code null/ Completed -> handed off, NO carrier response at all
# ---------------------------------------------------------------

REF = "$parse_input.message.incident_ref"
ACK_DIGIT = "$ack_digit".strip()

    try:
        v = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) and raw.strip() else None
        return v if isinstance(v, dict) else None
    except Exception:
        return None


plan = load(r"""$parse_input.message""") or {}

try:
    resp = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else raw
except Exception:
    resp = {}

rows = rows.get("data") if isinstance(rows, dict) else rows

    rows = []

    None check MUST come before any string coercion. str(None) is "None"
    - truthy and non-empty - which would pass Busy and undelivered calls
    as acknowledgments and stop the ladder with nobody woken up.

    if not cs.startswith(REF):

    # No history rows at all. Not "nobody answered" - we cannot even see
    # the calls. Auth, wrong window, or the API is down.

    out["outcome_line"] = ("NO CALL RECORDS - ClickSend history returned "

    out["outcome_line"] = ("NOT DELIVERED - %d of %d calls got no carrier "

comments.label: INPUT CONTRACT. Reads the exec argument from the calling workflow: incident_ref, message, numbers[]. Validates E.164 and fails loudly rather than paging nobody. On a MANUAL run there is no argument, so it falls back to oncall_numbers and reports input_source - the 'Failed finding exec' line is expected. Pre-builds all 8 ClickSend payloads.
LADDER STARTS. 5 calls to numbers[0], then 3 to numbers[1]. 70s apart, ~9 min worst case, ~EUR 0.40. TTS is en-gb/female, require_input=1, machine_detection=1.

DO NOT OPTIMISE. This queries the WHOLE incident window, not just its own call, so a late-recorded ack from an earlier stage is still caught here before the next call fires. Filtering by message_id would break that.

THE ACK DECISION - most likely thing to be broken later. ClickSend sends digits=null (not "") when no key was pressed. str(None) is "None", non-empty, so a naive check makes every Busy/unanswered call look ACKNOWLEDGED and nobody gets woken. The None check must come first.
HANDOFF. Stages 1-5 rang numbers[0] and got nothing. Stages 6-8 ring numbers[1]. If only one number was supplied, both halves target the same person.

UNCONDITIONAL EDGE - deliberate. Shuffle keeps only ONE branch per source/destination pair; a true/false pair here would silently collapse and the 'nobody answered' outcome would never reach Verdict. Verdict decides the outcome, not this edge.

RETURN CONTRACT. Each Eval emits the full verdict: {acknowledged, acked_by, digit, attempt, elapsed_seconds, stages_run, outcome, outcome_line, calls_line, attempts[]}. There is no collector node - the Eval that ends the ladder IS the result. outcome separates 'nobody answered' from 'nothing was delivered'; they need opposite responses at 04:00.

NO COLLECTOR NODE - ON PURPOSE. A single node reading all 8 Evals would error on the 7 that did not run and email you every time. Shuffle resolves variables textually, so any convergent node hits this. Each Eval is self-contained instead: Parse_Input + its own Poll, never another Eval.

name: NOSHUT SRIS_voice_ack
description:
REUSABLE SUBFLOW - phone escalation with keypress acknowledgment.

Call from any workflow with a Subflow node ('Wait for results' ON) and a JSON argument: {"incident_ref":"...","message":"...","numbers":["+351..."]}

Returns {acknowledged, acked_by, digit, attempt, elapsed_seconds, attempts}. Branch on .message.acknowledged equals true.

Ladder: 5 calls to numbers[0], then 3 to numbers[1], 70s apart. Stops on the first keypress.

Read the README node on the canvas before changing anything - especially the is_ack() null handling, which is what stops failed calls being counted as acknowledgments.
